=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/review_autofix_step_claude_fixer_judge.sh:107-120 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The rejection-marker selector accepts comments from any OWNER, MEMBER, or COLLABORATOR without binding the rejection to the fixing session’s identity, allowing a dispatch-capable collaborator to post the marker and bypass the reviewer panel.
  WHY: The gate narrows the set of actors who can bypass reviewers but does not prevent a collaborator who can dispatch from doing so; severity disagreement ranges from NIT to BLOCKER, with some reviewers noting this matches an approved design tradeoff.
- scripts/review_claude_fixer_judge.py:268-282, 310-323 | severity=critical | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Sticky invalid rulings are bound only to whether the finding’s cited file is unchanged, so a semantic change in another file can leave the ruling matching and demote a finding that is valid again.
  WHY: If that demotion removes the last counted finding, the changed head can be treated as clean and proceed toward auto-merge; severity disagreement is BLOCKER versus MAJOR.
- scripts/review_claude_fixer_judge.py:270-281 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `git_file_unchanged` does not catch `ValueError` from `subprocess.run`, which can propagate out of the sticky hand-off step if an argument contains an embedded null byte.
  WHY: The caller validates `head`, but `file_name` is unvalidated and could contain a null byte.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:2398-2411 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: `_rb_judge_guard_list` is removed only on the success path, leaving the temporary file behind on the two exit-1 paths.
  WHY: The file is a small temp file under TMPDIR and has no operational consequence.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:2400-2401 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: Sourcing `write_guard.sh` means future changes to that file will also execute in the Claude-fixer judge path.
  WHY: The reviewer says this matches the existing review-editor pattern and does not cross a new trust boundary; the risk is that a future regression in `write_guard.sh` affects both paths.
- changelog.d/6061-claude-fixer-judge-authorization-and-write-guards.md:line 2; README.md:line 90 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The headline says the judge needs the fixing session’s rejection, while the implementation accepts a collaborator’s rejection; README.md line 90 has the same overstatement.
  WHY: The headline and README description overstate the authorization scope, although the changelog body is accurate.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "#6061 — A `claude_fixer_judge_head` dispatch used to run the judge even when nobody had posted a rejection for that head and round, so anyone able to dispatch the workflow could have it skip the reviewers and merge. The judge now decides nothing without a collaborator's `ai:claude-fixer-rejection:v1` comment for that head and round" — i.e. the rejection must come from the *fixing session*, not from any collaborator.
  expected_change_site: scripts/review_autofix_step_claude_fixer_judge.sh — the rejection-selector branch that filters PR issue comments for the marker.
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The selector filters by `author_association` only; there is no check that the matching comment's `user.login` equals the PR author's login, equals `CLAUDE_FIXER_HANDOFF_AUTHOR_LOGIN` (the configured bot identity), or is otherwise an identity that a bare collaborator cannot impersonate. `test_prepare_refuses_a_dispatch_without_the_fixers_rejection` exercises empty / non-association / wrong-round cases but not the different-collaborator case. The changelog fragment's headline ("needs the fixing session's rejection to run") is broader than the implementation ("needs a collaborator's rejection").
- requirement: "#6062 — An `invalid` ruling from an earlier head kept hiding the same claim after the code changed. An `invalid` ruling demotes only while `git diff --quiet <ruled head> HEAD -- <file>` succeeds; any git doubt keeps the finding."
  expected_change_site: scripts/review_claude_fixer_judge.py — `git_file_unchanged` and its caller in `sticky`.
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The check is `git diff --quiet <head> HEAD -- <file_name>`, restricted to the cited file. A change outside the cited file (e.g. a caller, a shared module, a config flag) that makes the original finding valid again is not detected: the cited file is unchanged, the invalid ruling still matches, and the finding is demoted. A broader change-set binding (`git diff --quiet <head> HEAD` or a per-finding allow-list of relevant paths) is absent.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

  WHY: The code matches the approved AD-38 option A design, which chose collaborator-level authorization; the changelog headline overstates this as requiring the fixing session’s rejection, while the body is accurate.

- HARDENING_SUGGESTION: scripts/review_claude_fixer_judge.py:line 282 (git_file_unchanged exception handler). Add `ValueError` to the caught exceptions because `subprocess.run` can raise it for an embedded NUL byte. The reviewer says this cannot happen in practice given the validated head and ledger-parsed `file_name`; this would future-proof against library changes. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
